symptoms: The task dies with a Java stack, and the executor JVM reports the failure itself
The same job succeeded on a smaller input and fails as the input grows
One task fails repeatedly while the others in the same stage finish
likely_causes: A single task received far more data than its peers, so the heap that fits the others does not fit it
A broadcast join was chosen for a table that is no longer small
The job collects or materialises a large result on one side of the operation
diagnostic_steps: Compare max and median input bytes per task in the failing stage: heap exhaustion with an even distribution is a sizing problem, and with an uneven one it is skew
Read the physical plan for the join strategy of the failing stage
Read the effective spark.executor.memory and spark.memory.fraction; the Spark defaults are 1g and 0.6, and the second sets aside the rest for internal metadata
fixes: Treat the skew when the input distribution is uneven, because more heap pays the cost of the largest task on every executor
Disable or correct the broadcast decision when a table that grew is still being broadcast
Raise spark.executor.memory only after the distribution has been measured and found even
unsafe_fixes: Raising spark.memory.fraction above the default: the Spark documentation recommends leaving it alone and warns that raising it requires tuning JVM garbage collection as well
Raising heap while skew is present, which moves the failure without touching the cause and costs on every executor
verification: Re-run with the same input volume and confirm the stage completes; publish max/median input bytes per task before and after
rollback: Revert the memory override. If the fix changed the join key or the data distribution, the output has to be compared before the previous version is discarded
